# Introduction & Study Overview

This analysis investigates independent clinical and demographic factors associated with stroke fatality (`outcome`) using logistic regression in R. The study uses the dataset `stroke-fatality-cooked2.dta` (226 observations, 22 variables).

## Statistical Assumptions

1. **Binomial distribution** for the binary outcome (`0 = alive`, `1 = dead`).
2. **Linearity in the logit** for continuous independent variables.
3. **Correct model specification** without omission of critical confounders.

---

# Data Import, Cleaning & Validation

We load the required analytical libraries, read the Stata `.dta` file using the `haven` package, clean variable names using `janitor`, apply factor levels with descriptive labels, and verify data entry consistency.

```{r}
#| label: setup-and-import
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(gtsummary)
library(gt)
library(broom)
library(car)
library(MASS)
library(pROC)
library(ResourceSelection)

# Read raw dataset
stroke_raw <- read_dta("stroke-fatality-cooked2.dta")

# Clean column names
stroke_df <- stroke_raw %>% clean_names()

# Recode factor levels and numeric types
stroke_df <- stroke_df %>%
  mutate(
    outcome        = factor(outcome, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("alive", "dead")),
    sex            = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("male", "female")),
    hypertension   = factor(hypertension, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    maritalstat    = factor(maritalstat, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    malay          = factor(malay, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    diabetes       = factor(diabetes, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    dyslipidaemia  = factor(dyslipidaemia, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    referralcase   = factor(referralcase, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("hospital", "GP/Home/Missing")),
    stroketype     = factor(stroketype, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Ischaemic", "Haemorrhagic")),
    # Numeric variables
    across(c(gcs, sbp, dbp, hr, hb, plat, wbc, na, potas, cbs, urea, age), as.numeric)
  )

# Add binary 0/1 numeric outcome for modelling
stroke_df <- stroke_df %>%
  mutate(outcome_num = as.numeric(outcome) - 1)

glimpse(stroke_df)
```

## Missing Data & Range Checks

```{r}
#| label: data-quality-checks
# Missing data check
missing_summary <- stroke_df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Missing_Count") %>%
  mutate(Missing_Pct = round(Missing_Count / nrow(stroke_df) * 100, 2))

missing_summary %>%
  filter(Missing_Count > 0) %>%
  gt()

# Summary statistics for numerical variables
stroke_df %>%
  dplyr::select(gcs, sbp, dbp, hr, hb, plat, wbc, na, potas, cbs, urea, age) %>%
  summary()
```

The dataset contains complete observations ($N = 226$) across all 22 variables with **0 missing values**. Values fall within clinically plausible limits with one mild hypernatremia observation ($Na = 177\text{ mmol/L}$).

# Univariable Logistic Regression Analysis

We fit simple logistic regression models for each of the 20 candidate independent variables against `outcome_num`. Variables with a Wald test p-value $< 0.25$ are selected as candidates for the multivariable model.

```{r}
#| label: univariable-regression
iv_vars <- c("sex", "gcs", "sbp", "dbp", "hr", "hb", "plat", "wbc",
             "na", "potas", "cbs", "urea", "age",
             "hypertension", "maritalstat", "malay", "diabetes",
             "dyslipidaemia", "referralcase", "stroketype")

univar_results <- map_dfr(iv_vars, function(var) {
  form <- as.formula(paste("outcome_num ~", var))
  fit <- glm(form, data = stroke_df, family = binomial)
  
  tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = FALSE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(
      variable    = var,
      log_odds    = estimate,
      OR          = exp(estimate),
      OR_lower    = exp(conf.low),
      OR_upper    = exp(conf.high)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(variable, term, log_odds, std.error, OR, OR_lower, OR_upper, p.value)
})

# Display candidate table
univar_results %>%
  mutate(
    Selected_Candidate = if_else(p.value < 0.25, "Yes (p < 0.25)", "No"),
    across(c(log_odds, std.error, OR, OR_lower, OR_upper), ~ round(., 3)),
    p.value = if_else(p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Univariable Logistic Regression Results") %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable",
    term = "Parameter",
    log_odds = "Log-Odds (β)",
    std.error = "SE",
    OR = "Crude OR",
    OR_lower = "95% CI Lower",
    OR_upper = "95% CI Upper",
    p.value = "p-value",
    Selected_Candidate = "Selected (p < 0.25)"
  )

selected_vars <- univar_results %>%
  filter(p.value < 0.25) %>%
  pull(variable) %>%
  unique()

cat("Selected candidate variables for multivariable modelling:\n", paste(selected_vars, collapse = ", "))
```

---

# Multivariable Logistic Regression Analysis

## Multicollinearity Assessment

Before fitting the multivariable model, we examine the correlation matrix among continuous candidate predictors and inspect the Variance Inflation Factor (VIF).

```{r}
#| label: multicollinearity-check
cont_candidates <- intersect(selected_vars, c("gcs", "hr", "hb", "wbc", "na", "cbs"))
cor_mat <- cor(stroke_df[, cont_candidates], use = "complete.obs")
round(cor_mat, 3)

# Preliminary full candidate model for VIF
prelim_fit <- glm(as.formula(paste("outcome_num ~", paste(selected_vars, collapse = " + "))),
                  data = stroke_df, family = binomial)

vif_table <- tibble(
  Variable = names(vif(prelim_fit)),
  VIF = as.numeric(vif(prelim_fit))
)
vif_table %>% gt() %>% fmt_number(columns = VIF, decimals = 3)
```

All VIF values are well below 5 (maximum $\approx 1.62$), indicating no multicollinearity concerns.

## Variable Selection (Forward Likelihood Ratio Stepwise)

```{r}
#| label: stepwise-selection
null_model <- glm(outcome_num ~ 1, data = stroke_df, family = binomial)
full_formula <- as.formula(paste("outcome_num ~", paste(selected_vars, collapse = " + ")))

forward_model <- step(
  null_model,
  scope = list(lower = ~ 1, upper = full_formula),
  direction = "forward",
  test = "LRT",
  trace = 0
)

summary(forward_model)
```

## Exploration of Interaction Terms

We examine clinically meaningful two-way interactions:

```{r}
#| label: interaction-exploration
# Test interactions with GCS and Stroke Type
anova(forward_model, update(forward_model, ~ . + gcs:stroketype), test = "Chisq")
anova(forward_model, update(forward_model, ~ . + gcs:referralcase), test = "Chisq")

final_model <- forward_model
```

No interaction terms achieved statistical significance ($p > 0.05$). The forward LR model retaining **`gcs`** and **`sex`** is selected as the parsimonious final model.

---

# Overall Model Fitness & Evaluation

## Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) & AUC

```{r}
#| label: roc-auc
predicted_probs <- predict(final_model, type = "response")
roc_obj <- roc(stroke_df$outcome_num, predicted_probs, quiet = TRUE)
auc_ci <- ci.auc(roc_obj)

cat("AUC:", round(auc(roc_obj), 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI:", round(auc_ci[1], 4), "to", round(auc_ci[3], 4), "\n")

plot(roc_obj, main = paste("ROC Curve (AUC =", round(auc(roc_obj), 3), ")"),
     col = "#2563eb", lwd = 2.5, legacy.axes = TRUE,
     print.auc = TRUE, print.auc.x = 0.4, print.auc.y = 0.2)
```

## Hosmer-Lemeshow Goodness-of-Fit Test

```{r}
#| label: hosmer-lemeshow
hl_test <- hoslem.test(stroke_df$outcome_num, predicted_probs, g = 10)
hl_test
```

With $p = 0.099 > 0.05$, we fail to reject the null hypothesis, demonstrating adequate goodness of fit across risk deciles.

## Classification Accuracy & Model glance() using `broom`

```{r}
#| label: classification-accuracy
# Model-level glance
glance(final_model) %>% gt()

# Classification matrix with broom::augment
augmented_df <- augment(final_model, type.predict = "response") %>%
  mutate(predicted_class = if_else(.fitted >= 0.5, 1, 0))

conf_mat <- table(Predicted = augmented_df$predicted_class, Actual = augmented_df$outcome_num)
conf_mat

acc  <- sum(diag(conf_mat)) / sum(conf_mat)
sens <- conf_mat[2, 2] / sum(conf_mat[, 2])
spec <- conf_mat[1, 1] / sum(conf_mat[, 1])

tibble(
  Metric = c("Overall Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity"),
  Percentage = c(acc * 100, sens * 100, spec * 100)
) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = Percentage, decimals = 1, pattern = "{x}%")
```

---

# Diagnostic Statistics

We calculate diagnostic measures for all observations:

- **Leverage ($h_i$)**: Hat values ($\text{cutoff} = 2p/n = 0.0265$)
- **Delta-Beta ($\Delta\beta$)**: Cook's influence metric
- **Delta Chi-Square ($\Delta\chi^2$)**: Change in Pearson chi-square statistic
- **Delta Deviance ($\Delta D$)**: Change in model deviance

```{r}
#| label: diagnostic-plots
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
n <- nrow(stroke_df)
p <- length(coef(final_model))
leverage_cutoff <- 2 * p / n

diag_df <- augmented_df %>%
  mutate(
    obs_id        = row_number(),
    leverage      = .hat,
    cooks_d       = .cooksd,
    pearson_resid = (outcome_num - .fitted) / sqrt(.fitted * (1 - .fitted)),
    delta_chisq   = pearson_resid^2 / (1 - leverage),
    dev_resid     = sign(outcome_num - .fitted) *
                    sqrt(-2 * (outcome_num * log(.fitted) + (1 - outcome_num) * log(1 - .fitted))),
    delta_dev     = dev_resid^2 / (1 - leverage),
    delta_beta    = cooks_d * p
  )

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

# 1. Leverage
plot(diag_df$.fitted, diag_df$leverage,
     xlab = "Predicted Probability", ylab = "Leverage (hat value)",
     main = "Leverage vs Predicted Probability",
     pch = 16, col = ifelse(diag_df$leverage > leverage_cutoff, "red", "steelblue"))
abline(h = leverage_cutoff, lty = 2, col = "red")

# 2. Delta-beta
plot(diag_df$.fitted, diag_df$delta_beta,
     xlab = "Predicted Probability", ylab = "Delta-Beta (Δβ)",
     main = "Delta-Beta vs Predicted Probability",
     pch = 16, col = ifelse(abs(diag_df$delta_beta) > 1, "red", "steelblue"))
abline(h = c(-1, 1), lty = 2, col = "red")

# 3. Delta Chi-square
plot(diag_df$.fitted, diag_df$delta_chisq,
     xlab = "Predicted Probability", ylab = "Delta Chi-Square (Δχ²)",
     main = "Delta Chi-Square vs Predicted Probability",
     pch = 16, col = ifelse(diag_df$delta_chisq > 4, "red", "steelblue"))
abline(h = 4, lty = 2, col = "red")

# 4. Delta Deviance
plot(diag_df$.fitted, diag_df$delta_dev,
     xlab = "Predicted Probability", ylab = "Delta Deviance (ΔD)",
     main = "Delta Deviance vs Predicted Probability",
     pch = 16, col = ifelse(diag_df$delta_dev > 4, "red", "steelblue"))
abline(h = 4, lty = 2, col = "red")
```

# Final Combined Results & Clinical Summary

```{r}
#| label: combined-results-table
univar_table_data <- univar_results %>%
  mutate(
    uni_log_odds = sprintf("%.3f", log_odds),
    uni_OR       = sprintf("%.3f", OR),
    uni_CI       = sprintf("%.3f – %.3f", OR_lower, OR_upper),
    uni_p        = if_else(p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, term, uni_log_odds, uni_OR, uni_CI, uni_p)

multi_tidy <- tidy(final_model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = FALSE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    multi_log_odds = sprintf("%.3f", estimate),
    multi_OR       = sprintf("%.3f", exp(estimate)),
    multi_CI       = sprintf("%.3f – %.3f", exp(conf.low), exp(conf.high)),
    multi_p        = if_else(p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(term, multi_log_odds, multi_OR, multi_CI, multi_p)

combined_table <- univar_table_data %>%
  left_join(multi_tidy, by = "term") %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("multi_"), ~ replace_na(., "—")))

combined_table %>%
  dplyr::select(-term) %>%
  rename(
    Variable           = variable,
    `Log-odds (β)`     = uni_log_odds,
    `OR`               = uni_OR,
    `95% CI`           = uni_CI,
    `p-value`          = uni_p,
    `Log-odds (β) `    = multi_log_odds,
    `OR `              = multi_OR,
    `95% CI `          = multi_CI,
    `p-value `         = multi_p
  ) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Univariable Logistic Regression", columns = c(`Log-odds (β)`, `OR`, `95% CI`, `p-value`)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Multivariable Logistic Regression", columns = c(`Log-odds (β) `, `OR `, `95% CI `, `p-value `)) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Logistic Regression of Stroke Fatality",
    subtitle = "Crude and Adjusted Odds Ratios with 95% Confidence Intervals"
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote("Reference levels: Sex = male; Stroke type = Ischaemic; Referral = Hospital; Binary comorbidities = no.")
```

## Summary of Findings

1. **Glasgow Coma Scale (`gcs`)**: Strongest independent protective factor ($\text{AOR} = 0.489$, $95\%\text{ CI: } 0.396 - 0.588$, $p < 0.001$). Higher consciousness at presentation substantially reduces the probability of stroke mortality.
2. **Patient Sex (`sex`)**: Female stroke patients had lower in-hospital mortality odds compared to male patients ($\text{AOR} = 0.327$, $95\%\text{ CI: } 0.100 - 0.945$, $p = 0.044$) after controlling for GCS.
3. **Discriminative Capacity**: The final model achieves outstanding discrimination ($\text{AUC} = 0.943$) and satisfactory calibration ($p = 0.099$).
